why_this_matters: Day 218 sits in Phase 12 (Deep Learning + Computer Vision), whose goal is: Understand neural networks from a single neuron to a trained CNN. Today's core material - Underfitting vs overfitting learning curves, L1/L2 weight decay, Dropout mechanics and inference behaviour - is the vocabulary the rest of the phase is built on. Learners who skip the concept and jump to copying code usually stall two weeks later; the goal here is that you can explain what you did, not just that it ran.

code.heading: 5. L1/L2 Regularization
code.code:
from tensorflow.keras.layers import Dense, Flatten, Dropout
from tensorflow.keras.models import Sequential
from tensorflow.keras.regularizers import l1, l2, l1_l2
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Define a model with L1 regularization
def create_model_with_l1():
    model = Sequential([
        Flatten(input_shape=(28, 28)),
        Dense(128, activation='relu', kernel_regularizer=l1(0.0001)),  # L1 regularization
        Dropout(0.5), # Adding dropout which will also be regularized by L1
        Dense(10, activation='softmax')
    ])
    model.compile(optimizer='adam',
                  loss='sparse_categorical_crossentropy',
                  metrics=['accuracy'])
    return model

# Define a model with L2 regularization
def create_model_with_l2():
    model = Sequential([
        Flatten(input_shape=(28, 28)),
        Dense(128, activation='relu', kernel_regularizer=l2(0.0001)),  # L2 regularization
        Dropout(0.5), # Adding dropout which will also be regularized by L2
        Dense(10, activation='softmax')
    ])
    model.compile(optimizer='adam',
                  loss='sparse_categorical_crossentropy',
                  metrics=['accuracy'])
    return model

# should we combine them both?
# Define a model with L1_L2 (combined) regularization
def create_model_with_l1_l2():
    model = Sequential([
        Flatten(input_shape=(28, 28)),
        Dense(128, activation='relu', kernel_regularizer=l1_l2(l1=0.0001, l2=0.0001)),  # L1_L2 regularization
        Dropout(0.5), # Adding dropout which will also be regularized by L1_L2
        Dense(10, activation='softmax')
    ])
    model.compile(optimizer='adam',
                  loss='sparse_categorical_crossentropy',
                  metrics=['accuracy'])
    return model

common_mistakes.mistake: Watching the lecture without running the repository notebook.
common_mistakes.why: Recognition is not recall: code that looked obvious fails the moment you type it yourself.
common_mistakes.fix: For every topic today, run the linked notebook cell, then retype it from memory in your own file.

common_mistakes.mistake: Using Underfitting vs overfitting learning curves on data whose types or shape you have not printed.
common_mistakes.why: Most failures in this topic are input problems (dtype, shape, missing values) rather than logic errors.
common_mistakes.fix: Print type and shape immediately before the operation; keep that habit for all 275 days.

debugging.symptom: The linked notebook cell raises ModuleNotFoundError or ImportError.
debugging.cause: Wrong kernel/environment selected, or the library is not installed in the active environment.
debugging.fix: Print sys.executable in the notebook and install into that environment (Day 4).

debugging.symptom: Your output differs from the recording even though the code looks identical.
debugging.cause: Library version differences, a changed default argument, or unseeded randomness.
debugging.fix: Pin versions (requirements.txt), set a random seed, and compare dtypes and shapes, not just values (Day 5).
